Exact MySQL effect of INSERT ... SELECT UUID(), id ... FROM site_builder_sites WHERE restaurant_id=? ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE status='active', ssl_status='active' (keys: PRIMARY id, uk_domain): (a) mapping for the domain already exists -> every selected row conflicts; only status/ssl_status change (and updated_at via ON UPDATE only if they changed); site_id, is_primary, id untouched; all generated UUIDs discarded. (b) no mapping yet -> FIRST row in the SELECT's scan order is inserted (its site_id and a fresh UUID), every later row conflicts on uk_domain and only re-sets status/ssl_status to the same values (no change). MySQL scan order depends on the chosen access path (idx_restaurant_id -> (restaurant_id,id) order, i.e. smallest id first) - not runtime-proven. PG branch uses LIMIT 1 with NO ORDER BY: case (a) identical; case (b) the chosen site_id may differ from MySQL's first-scanned row. Not equivalent; candidate source-faithful options (not applied, need decision/evidence): ORDER BY id under the MySQL-equivalent collation, or a two-step insert-first-then-update. Row counts: one mapping row in both; affected-row counts unused (errors ignored).
